Added an in-flight check to POST /v1/jobs/{name} (internal/lineupapi/handler.go handleJob + jobs.go inFlightRun): before launching, scans recent runs for a RUNNING entry whose command's first token matches the requested job name, and rejects with 409 if found. Matches on base job name (ignoring flags) per the acceptance criteria's 'same job name' wording, since the race (e.g. claims cursor) isn't specific to one param combination. Bounded by a 2h staleness window since entrypoint.sh only flips RUNNING->SUCCESS/FAILED after the command exits -- a hard crash mid-run would otherwise leave a ledger entry RUNNING forever and permanently block future manual triggers for that job, which would have been a worse regression than the race it fixes. Fails open (nil RunStore or a List error skips the check) since this is a race-reduction guard, not a strict lock, and local  runs without Runs configured at all. 8 new tests covering the pure inFlightRun logic (name matching, staleness, fail-open paths) plus full handler-level 409/202 wiring.

Root cause: internal/backtest reuses the live optimizer as a hindsight engine; optimalAssignment fills every slot it can and only leaves one empty when no eligible player remains — correct for projections (never negative), wrong for realised FPts. On 2026-07-02 only 2 pitchers had games against 6 P slots, so a -9.00 RESERVE (Roki Sasaki) was activated into a free slot; hitters lost another point to Jake Bauers at -1. Optimal 41 vs actual 48 = Gap +7. Not cause 1/2/3 from the issue description. Fix (PR #94->#97, merged 6840f80): hindsightValue floors each player at max(0, FPts) — benching yields exactly 0 and is always available, so the floor IS the achievable optimum and makes optimal>=actual provable. Kept out of optimalAssignment to avoid changing live tie-breaks (empty-slot branches would grow ToBench and churn the roster) and slowing the search. guardOptimal clamps any residual violation to actual with a stderr warning. Verified: full season 2026-03-26..08-02 (130 days) zero positive gaps; 13 of 42 days in 06-16..07-27 were understated, efficiency 76.2%->74.6%. NOT A BUG (PR #99, 34da92b). No behavior change; the derivation is now written into gs_budget.go so it doesn't get refiled. Defect (1): the fractional tail's 'placeholder * weight' is NOT a units error. The weight belongs in the price precisely BECAUSE the cut spends a whole slot — the gate's question is marginal (hold this slot or spend it today?), holding is worth placeholder*min(E,1) in expectation, spending is worth the starter's value with certainty, and those are the two quantities that must be comparable. Counterexample against the prescribed full-value form: 1 slot left, certain 8-pt start today, 0.2 expected future starts at a 12-pt placeholder — full-value pricing benches the 8 to hold a slot that materializes 20%% of the time (2.4 expected vs 8 certain), and weekly GS is use-it-or-lose-it so the other 80%% is burned, not banked. The issue is also internally inconsistent: a LARGER certaintyMargin makes estimated-future outrank today LESS often, which spends more budget today — the opposite of the under-reserving it groups with rosterbot-abd. Defect (2): re-deriving certaintyMargin from SP projection MAE does not hold — that dispersion is symmetric, and haircutting an unbiased estimate biases the ranking rather than de-risking it. What the margin actually prices is P(the estimated start never materializes); now documented, along with the fact that 0.10 is an unmeasured prior. Measuring it split out to rosterbot-xsm. Tests: TestApplyGSGate_EstimatedLadderPricesWholeUnitsFullAndTailMarginally pins both rungs (E=1.4 -> 12.0 and 4.8); verified discriminating by mutation (pricing the tail at full value fails it and TestApplyGSGate_FractionalEstimateDoesNotOverSuppressToday).

Fixed in PR #99 (34da92b). Filtered in the display aggregation (topBenchCumulative), NOT at the source: benchedPoints keeps negative scorers because len(Benched) is persisted daily as lineupgap.Row.BenchedN ('scored but not started') in the durable Lineup Gap Store, so filtering there would silently redefine that series mid-season and make new dt= partitions incomparable to old ones. topBenchCumulative still aggregates every bench day including negatives, so the total stays a player's NET counterfactual (+10 Mon / -9 Tue = +1 left behind, not +10); only the net is required positive (<= 0 dropped, so an exactly-zero net is excluded too). Filtering before the top-10 truncation means the section shows ten real misses when ten exist rather than spending slots on avoided losses. ActualPts/OptimalPts/Gap untouched. Tests: TestBuildReport_TopBenchExcludesNetNegative (reproduces the Sasaki -9.00 row, asserts per-day Benched still carries it) and TestBuildReport_TopBenchNetsAcrossDaysBeforeFiltering; both verified discriminating by mutation.

Pruned 2,542 orphaned pre-season-scoping objects (24.3 MiB) from the S3 cache/ prefix on 2026-08-03; cache/ went 5,260 -> 2,718 objects, 91.3 -> 67.0 MiB. Verified before deleting: (a) all six renamed key families build through seasonScopedKey, so the old grammar is unreachable in code; (b) no orphan had been modified since 2026-07-31 while new-grammar keys were written through today — a clean cutover at the rename commit; (c) a live recap --dates 2026-07-27:2026-08-02 against STATE_BUCKET touched 1,390 keys in those six families and ZERO in the old grammar (the acceptance criterion's warm build — today's scheduled Monday Recap had died on STALE_CLIENT, so this was also the first successful post-rename recap). Delete list guard-checked to exclude new-grammar keys, the unscoped todayTTL roster keys, and anything non-fantrax. Bucket is versioned, so the objects remain restorable until the existing 14-day ExpireNoncurrentCacheVersions rule reclaims them.

Decided AGAINST the notes' alternative of a general lifecycle rule on cache/: PastPeriodTTL objects are meant to be kept forever (that is the whole point of rosterbot-qoa), so an expiration rule there would delete live cache and reintroduce the superlinear recap-site cost qoa fixed. The one-off prune was the right instrument; the noncurrent-version rule already covers the versioning half of the storage-audit gap.

Follow-up filed: rosterbot-sza — InvalidatePeriodRosterCache still builds the pre-rename key grammar and so has invalidated nothing since 2026-07-31. Found via this prune: the keys it deletes ARE these orphans.

Fixed by routing both sides through one key builder rather than correcting the key. periodCacheKey(prefix, teamID, period) now returns the key and its tier from a single periodCachePolicy read; cachedForPeriod and InvalidatePeriodRosterCache both call it, so the writer and the invalidator cannot drift again — which was the actual defect, not the wrong string.

Confirmed the bug behaviourally before fixing: the new test fails red against the old code with 2 fetches where 3 were expected, i.e. the invalidation dropped nothing. It drives the real reader (cachedForPeriod, what GetHitterRosterForPeriod calls) instead of comparing key strings, because a string comparison would have to be rewritten to match any future refactor and would keep passing while the behaviour broke. A second test pins the current-day keys, which carry no season by design (todayTTL, no period number) and had to keep the plain grammar — the fix must not sweep them into season scoping and break them the other way.
